creator: buildwithneej
title: Paperclip: open-source repo that runs AI coding agents as a company with an org chart (CEO/CTO/engineers), heartbeat scheduling, budgets and one dashboard

tools.name: Paperclip
tools.detail: Open-source, 'over 90,000 stars'; installs locally in about a minute; dashboard with agents, assignments, budget approvals

tools.name: Claude (Claude Code)
tools.detail: Org chart: 'CEO runs on Claude', 'CTO runs on Claude', 'ClaudeCoder runs on Claude'

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.detail: One org-chart node 'runs on Codex' -- you pick which AI runs each role

claims: Repo has over 90,000 GitHub stars 'at the moment' and is free
You write one goal; the CEO agent hires the team (CTO, engineers, designers, marketers) on its own; you set the budget, approve, hit go
Every agent runs on a heartbeat: wakes on a schedule, checks its work, acts or goes back to sleep
Installs locally in about a minute; one dashboard replaces babysitting agents across many terminals
how_to_steps: Pick which model/agent runtime powers each role (Claude, Codex, etc.)
CEO agent proposes hires; set a budget and approve
Hit go and watch agents on the dashboard; they run on heartbeat schedules
on_screen_only: Title card: 'Turn Claude into a whole AI Company'
Org chart: CEO (runs on Claude) -> CTO (runs on Claude), [role] (runs on Codex), ClaudeCoder (runs on Claude)
List: CTO / ENGINEERS / DESIGNERS / MARKETERS -- each tagged 'hired' -- 'whoever the goal needs'
Paperclip dashboard: sidebar with agents (CEO, CTO, ...), CEO page with 'Assign Task' / 'Pause' buttons, bar charts (Run Activity, Agent Activity?, Budget), 'Recent Issues' list, 'Checking'
cta: Comment 'Company' to get the repo link by DM

relevance.why: Multi-agent orchestration with budgets and heartbeats is interesting for a solo founder who wants work to continue unattended, but a CEO/CTO hierarchy of agents is mostly theatre; the useful bits (scheduled wake-ups, budget caps, single dashboard) can be done with Claude Code routines/subagents already.

implement_score.why: Not worth adopting wholesale: adds a heavy framework and token burn for an org-chart metaphor. Worth 30 minutes to read the repo for the heartbeat + budget-approval pattern and maybe reuse the idea in our own scheduled Claude Code routines.

verify: Find the actual repo (owner/paperclip) and verify the 90k-star claim -- that is enormous and may be inflated
Which agent runtimes it supports (Claude Code, Codex CLI, others) and how it meters budget
Token cost of idle heartbeats; security of agents with repo/shell access
